label: Street's dilemma extended to epistemic reasons: realist self-application and survivors
summary: #1585. Materialized the pinned Street 2006 witness and read n. 2 (p. 156) and n. 57 (pp. 163–164) with context: Street states she thinks the dilemma extends to realism about epistemic reasons, does not argue it, and says her alien-investigator reply to self-application assumes shared judgments about epistemic reasons, a complication she leaves undiscussed. Two stating claims record exactly this. Analyst reconstruction, attribution deferred: a Darwinian profile for one scoped epistemic evaluative judgment separates origin fixing, within-history variation of correctness, tracking failure (a wrong verdict in some scenario with the actual history), justified defeat (undercutting in the existing ReliabilityFrame) and global epistemic nihilism. Verified: (1) origin fixing plus within-history variation yields a tracking failure by case split on actual accuracy; (2) with the debunker's mismatch-undercuts policy stated uniformly over bases, the same premises for the debunker's own epistemic basis, sole-basis dependence and warrant-needs-undefeated-support give lack of warrant for the debunking conclusion, reusing undercutSoleBasisPrecludesWarrant; (3) history-fixed correctness with an accurate selection-fixed verdict keeps every history-mate accurate; (4) finite controls: tracking failure with actual accuracy, variation without origin fixing gives no failure, the realist self-application premises are jointly satisfiable with the conclusion true and thin F6 intact, and an antirealist debunker accepting the same policy keeps warrant. Self-application result: the realist who accepts the uniform policy and relies on an epistemic basis whose correctness varies within its history is epistemically self-undermined, not strictly self-refuting; the conclusion may be true. Antirealism alone yields no contradiction (control 5). Strongest surviving replies: (a) constructivism about epistemic reasons, on which correctness is fixed by the attitudes the history fixes, so the debunker keeps warrant; it extends the antirealist reply of n. 57 to epistemic reasons, and no source for that extension was read here; (b) a necessitarian or supervenience realism on which stance-independent epistemic correctness necessarily supervenes on descriptive truth-conduciveness, which selection responds to, so the within-history variation premise fails and the extended dilemma does not reach that realism; (c) the independent-basis reply (n. 57's alien) attacks sole-basis dependence, but for epistemic reasons the considerations the alien weighs are themselves assessed by epistemic standards, which is exactly the complication Street flags; whether some non-evaluative basis can support the conclusion is open. Frontier delta: no change (476 open premises reaching the root before and after). Root connection plan: F6 is a floor item and these results neither use nor threaten its thin existential; the route to the case runs through warrant for accepting root-route premises, the #930 bridge that remains unbuilt.
blocker: Whether the correctness of any actual epistemic evaluative judgment varies within our selective history (the realist premise) and whether the uniform mismatch-undercuts policy is a correct defeat principle are open; sole-basis dependence of the debunking conclusion is open; the #930 bridge from epistemic warrant to acceptance of root-route premises is unbuilt. Next test: formalize the supervenience realism profile with descriptive truth-conduciveness as an explicit input and test whether a weaker, non-modal reliability premise still gives defeat without the variation premise.
